concepts.definition: A customer's request to purchase goods.
concepts.lifecycle: Created pending; becomes confirmed after acceptance.

invariants.statement: The order id remains unchanged through confirmation.

components.responsibility: Collect an order and display confirmation
Accept orders and retain their state
allowed_effects: Store orders through its owned persistence adapter

contracts.description: Small example payload shared by both sides

interfaces.behavior: Send a pending order; display the returned confirmed order.
Accept pending order, retain confirmed state and return the same id.

connections.behavior: POST the order; return the stored confirmation.

mappings.representation: Use the same id in the API response and orders table; retain it during state changes.

obligations.check: Assert that the confirmation and stored state retain the submitted order id.

scenarios.setup: Empty store and synthetic pending order order-1.

steps.expect: A confirmed response with id order-1; store contains that same confirmation.

scenarios.outcome: The user sees confirmation of the order retained by the service.

questions: This teaching slice omits failures, repeated requests and persistence ports. Complete the project's actual graph and scenario scope before constructing it.
